method: Worker visual review of the numbered 66-candidate contact sheet at equal rendered height; rank is editorial, not an automatic anatomical score. Preserve identity, age and natural build if the owner chooses regeneration.

topTen.reason: Broad, rounded head and face over a compact torso/shorter legs; reads as a different caricature style beside the slimmer founder.
Large rounded head/hair silhouette and compact lower body; the head-to-limb balance remains visibly different after height matching.
Wide head/hair mass and short lower-body silhouette. Hair contributes to the automated estimate, but the whole silhouette difference is visible.
Wide squared head/bob and compressed neck/torso proportions give a more chibi silhouette than the founder.
Rounded oversized head and shorter leg-to-torso balance; distinguish this stylistic issue from preserving a naturally broad build.
Broad, round head with compact torso/legs; reads as a different batch style at the same full height.
Small realistic head on a long torso/leg silhouette; the opposite proportion mismatch from the large-head batches.
Relatively small head and broad torso/shoulders. Similar to the reported red-sweater X-ray occupant; height normalization alone does not narrow this silhouette.
Green-scrub imaging technician has a broad torso and smaller head-to-body balance than the founder; directly relevant to the X-ray comparison.
Small realistic head above a broad torso; height-fringe repair fixes size but leaves the batch's head/body style difference.

bakedPeople.limitation: Side-lying patient plus blanket is inseparable from the bed. Projected cover length is not anatomical standing height; do not resize the furniture to force a band.
Side-lying patient is baked into the occupied bed. A pose-specific transparent patient overlay would need new art; all bed pixels and contacts must be retained.
Head and feet are covered; only a drape extent and abdominal window are visible. Full figure height cannot be measured or certified from this asset. Never shrink the entire OR table.
